prologue.tagline: Hold up your phone and find the voices from a hundred years ago hidden around Kumamoto University.
prologue.step1.title: Find
prologue.step1.body: Visit 3 places on campus: the Chemistry Laboratory, Goko Café (festival stall) and the Goko Memorial Museum. Any order is fine.
prologue.step2.title: Scan
prologue.step2.body: Scan the QR code with your phone's built-in Camera app.
prologue.step3.title: Claim
prologue.step3.body: Once you have all 3 stamps, exchange them for the prize “Pukuseki (Puku-Ishi)” (a limited balloon) at the Goko Memorial Museum.

guide.title: Goko Guide ({n} / 4)
guide.1.t: Check your stamps and secret words
guide.1.b: Tap the stamp book at the top right to see the stamps you've collected and your “4 secret words.”
guide.2.t: Explore the school of a hundred years ago
guide.2.b: Tap a building on the map to read a story from a hundred years ago. Head for the blinking pins and look for the QR codes.

food.where: The stall is between the Goko Memorial Museum and the Bunpo Building, near the roundabout and the Sub Stage. A clue to the “whisper” is hidden on the booth sign or on the cups.
food.about: Goko Café is a food stall run during this year's SIGMA Festival. It is not a historic café.
food.item.akane.name: Sunset Cream Soda
food.item.akane.title: Sunset Cream Soda (Akanezora)
food.item.akane.short: A glass of sunset-red soda topped with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.akane.desc: A cream soda whose sunset-red color fills the glass. Enjoy the smooth vanilla ice cream with the fizzy bubbles.
food.item.aoi.name: Blue Sky Cream Soda
food.item.aoi.title: Blue Sky Cream Soda (Aozora)
food.item.aoi.short: A refreshing soda in a clear blue gradient, served with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.aoi.desc: An eye-catching drink that fades from deep blue to sky blue. The cup carries a special commemorative sticker from Goko Café. Enjoy the fizz and the smooth ice cream.
food.item.shin.name: Fresh Green Cream Soda
food.item.shin.title: Fresh Green Cream Soda (Shinryoku)
food.item.shin.short: A nostalgic café classic: vivid emerald green topped with a bright red cherry.
food.item.shin.desc: A classic cream soda that recalls the Western-style café culture of the Meiji era. Look for the red cherry and the special cat sticker. A perfect break during your walk.
food.item.yugi.name: Evening Mist Cream Soda
food.item.yugi.title: Evening Mist Cream Soda (Yugiri)
food.item.yugi.short: A cream soda in soft colors like mist at dusk, served with vanilla ice cream.
food.item.yugi.desc: A cream soda with soft colors like evening mist spreading through the glass. Enjoy the smooth vanilla ice cream with the fizzy bubbles.

place.chem.summary: A red-brick laboratory. The first voice sleeps in the QR code here.
place.chem.title: Lamp-driven airflow and the one-sided corridor for the afternoon sun
place.chem.body: In 1889 (Meiji 22), before electricity was available, this building used the rising heat of lamps to carry toxic gases up the chimney. The exhaust system (a draft chamber, or fume hood) still survives and is one of the oldest of its kind in Japan. To block Kumamoto's strong afternoon sun, a long corridor was built only along the west side.
place.goko.summary: A memorial museum with an arched entrance. The last voice sleeps here.
place.goko.title: The weight of red brick and Greek columns
place.goko.body: The solid red-brick walls, laid in English bond, are about 60 cm (2 ft) thick on the first floor. The grand central staircase is decorated with graceful columns in the Greek style. The building still shows traces of the school where Natsume Soseki and Lafcadio Hearn once taught.
place.cafe.summary: Go to the Food page for Goko Café (festival stall).
place.relief.summary: A relief carved on the wall.
place.relief.title: The “Kumamoto spirit” given to students
place.gate.summary: The gate at the campus entrance.
place.gate.name: Front Gate (“Akamon”, the Red Gate)
place.gate.title: Through the stern gate, buckwheat in bloom
place.gate.body: The front gate was built in 1889 (Meiji 22) facing the old Bungo Road, and it has never had doors. Beyond the sturdy red-brick gate lay a field on the school grounds, which Natsume Soseki captured in the haiku “Through the stern gate, buckwheat in bloom.”
cele.honkan.lines: Wrapped in a hundred years of wind, the red brick still keeps quiet time. / Every step you took opens a page of a new era.
cele.honkan.source: Former Fifth High School, Memorial Museum Main Building
cele.hearn.lines: A foreign wind blows through this garden, and the spirit of old Japan lives on. / To you, who set aside needless luxury and sought honest truth.
cele.soseki.lines: Education is the foundation of a nation, and harmony between teacher and student is the root of nurturing talent. / We honor your journey, which touched a century of learning and deepened your thinking.
cele.soseki.source: From Natsume Soseki's address at the Fifth High School commemoration ceremony
cele.tea.lines: In this school of the Land of Fire, the wisdom of East and West meets warmly. / To you, who has heard every voice: our highest praise, and a cup to go with it.
cele.tea.source: A Crossing of Wisdom: Goko Café (festival stall)
place.relief.body: A bronze bas-relief of Lafcadio Hearn standing as if watching over the red-brick Main Building. The stone monument beside it is inscribed with the concluding words of his address to students, urging them to preserve the spirit of Kyushu and Kumamoto—'loving simple strength, simplicity, and goodness.'
whisper.1.lines: Approach through intellect, and edges grow sharp; / Paddle with emotion, and you are swept away. / Force your will, and life becomes confined. / Climbing the mountain path, / Such were the thoughts that stirred my mind.
whisper.2.lines: I am a cat—and still without a name. / As for where I came into the world, / I haven't the faintest notion; / Yet the lively bustle of this seat of learning / Suits me remarkably well.
whisper.3.lines: The spirit of old Japan still breathes here. / O pure and tranquil garden, / The voices of youthful companions / Are carved into these centenary stones.
consent.doc.body:
• We collect: the nickname you set, stamp progress, and technical logs needed to keep the service secure.
• We do not collect: real name, email, phone number, or detailed GPS location.
• Data is used only to run the stamp rally, verify prize exchange, and keep the system stable.
• Server-side records are deleted within 30 days after the festival ends.
• Anonymous statistics (e.g. total participants) may be used in campus museum reports.
• Misuse (inappropriate nicknames, abuse of the system) may result in deletion of records without notice.
• Contact: Campus Museum Promotion Organization, Kumamoto University (email as shown on this screen).
• The Japanese Terms of Use and Privacy Policy are the authoritative text; this is a summary for convenience.
